column1: 389093|heisenberg|A–C and references|All three requests remain in scope. The text distinguishes quantum ferro/antiferromagnets and explicitly notes failure of reflection positivity for the former. Ground-state ferromagnetic alignment is already printed and cannot settle positive-temperature order or robustness. No cheap uniform infrared replacement identified.

389096|fermi|Hamiltonian, density matrix, attractive spinning paragraph|The body fixes weak coupling, smooth finite-range interactions and a thermodynamic/zero-temperature limit. Repulsive and spinless Luttinger results do not give the attractive spinful asymptotic or its coupling dependence. No controlled nontrivial-fixed-point mechanism identified.

389101|bose-detail|Hamiltonian and C_Psi definition|The free gas W=0 is an internal example, not a resolution of the interacting request. Full scope needs a volume-uniform positive condensate fraction for repulsive interaction; lattice half-density is explicitly only background. No cheap interacting lower bound identified.

389108|simon|2000 list entry; primary PDF TLS failure|Secondary statement only. Ionization asymptotics require control of the difference of neighboring many-electron energies; a leading total-energy asymptotic does not provide that control. Primary conventions and sign/index correspondence remain unverified; access failure is not hardness evidence.

389110|simon|2000 list entry; primary PDF TLS failure|Secondary statement only. Molecular-configuration justification has no single quantified error regime in the assigned wording. Must recover the primary formulation before defining a theorem; a favorable molecule or Born-Oppenheimer heuristic would not solve full scope. No ineligibility inferred.

389113|simon|2000 list entry; primary PDF TLS failure|Secondary statement only. The entire open exponent interval and optimal constant are requested; endpoint inequalities or a single potential cannot settle it. Primary normalization and successor theorem bodies are not cleared, so no investment or novelty claim.

389134|quantum|Problem 2, Section II.B|Both alternatives are literal: four bases suffice for construction, while nonexistence branch concerns seven. The body supplies Hadamard formulation and product-basis obstructions, not a general obstruction. Restricting to product bases or a chosen Hadamard family leaves a gap. No exact witness or full obstruction found.

389135|quantum|Problem 4, Section III.A and Werner-state reduction|The body defines distillation via some finite tensor power; bound entanglement requires failure at every power. One-copy nondistillability and negative partial transpose are insufficient. The Werner reduction is source-reported, not independently dependency-audited. No all-power mechanism identified.

389141|mccurley|C7/O7a and Rem7|Input length is logarithmic in integer n. Polynomial squarefree decomposition using gcd with a derivative is explicitly a different domain in the source. Factoring n first gives no deterministic polynomial-time bound. No new full algorithm or lower-bound mechanism.

389165|mccurley|C27/O27 and Rem27|Source asks polynomial time for arbitrary prime field and admissible order, not merely point counting. Supersingular order p+1 examples are already printed. General CM enumeration does not supply a deterministic polynomial-in-log-p guarantee. Related r389289 is grouped, not proposed twice.

389167|mccurley|C29/O29, Euclidean norm and variable dimension|The source distinguishes other norms and fixed-dimensional algorithms. Need a reduction for the variable-dimensional Euclidean search problem with the intended deterministic/randomized reduction convention. No successor proof body was audited, so neither resolution nor novelty is asserted from remembered NP-hardness results.

389168|mccurley|C30/O30 and LLL comparison|The required n^c factor has a fixed c and polynomial time in variable dimension. Printed exponential approximation bounds do not bridge that gap; fixed-dimensional exact SVP does not help. No polynomial-factor method identified.

389180|dn|Section 3.2|The body supplies D(256) and D(-255) quintuples, hence bounds only. Full request needs both extremal parameters and exclusions of all nearer values, not another tuple at one n. No cheap global nonexistence certificate; no search launched.

389185|gener|Section 7.2, polynomial nondegeneracy and bounds|The primary page defines the common-scaling exclusion and reports degree-zero, linear and quadratic bounds 22,12,98. Full degree-only bound for arbitrary degree needs a coefficient-independent bridge; specializing those cases or rescaling constant tuples would not supply it. No such bridge identified.

389212|complexity|Conjecture 3.13 and preceding Nullstellensatz paragraph|The survey prints the Bezout coefficient-output lower-bound conjecture. Must fix computation model and input/output representation before a complexity proof. Exponential-degree examples alone need an explicit encoding/output lower-bound bridge; no full mechanism or novelty clearance established.

389230|complexity|Problem 4.6 and preceding L(V) definition|L is the infimum of normalized Mahler measure over nonzero noncyclotomic algebraic numbers with all conjugates outside the sector. Nine angular values are already reported known. Computing one more example or bound does not determine the full theta-function; no sharp all-angle certificate identified.

389247|howe|Frey Problem 1, arithmetic duality context|The actual body is Frey's duality talk despite the local filename. Bilinearity alone is not cryptographic usefulness: efficient representations and operations also matter. The source's existing arithmetic pairings are background; no new complete construction and security bridge identified.

389248|howe|Frey Problem 2, Pic(O) realization|All three conditions must hold together: embedding of a large prime cyclic group, compact representatives and O(log ell) composition. Class-group existence alone or a large representation fails full scope. No new uniform construction with complexity proof identified.

389250|howe|Frey Problem 3 and Theorem 2.2 application|The source proposes realizing finite-field multiplicative subgroups via Picard groups and asks explicitness and security under Weil descent. A descent map alone is not an attack or preservation proof. The cited structural theorem was not dependency-audited; security model and concrete realization need further source work.

389251|howe|Frey Problem 4 and good-reduction/root-of-unity case|The source already says yes under good reduction and n dividing q-1 and supplies a cocycle expression. Reproducing that case earns no credit. Removing these restrictions requires the local algebra and representation bridge, not merely a fast finite-field pairing subroutine; no full algorithm identified.

389253|howe|Frey Problems 5–6, generalized-dihedral splitting|The requested cocycle c_u and local invariants concern the generalized-dihedral extension described in the talk. Known cyclic local duality only proves an equivalence/existence, not the required fast explicit conversion. No cheap cocycle conversion identified.

389254|howe|Frey Problem 7, globalization of algebras|Need explicit construction matching specified local Brauer data, with global compatibility and useful splitting presentation. Abstract global existence alone does not satisfy explicitness, and the cyclic subsection cannot silently replace dihedral input. No full constructive bridge identified.

389255|kedlaya-actual|Schoof discussion, slides 5–6|The body explicitly asks simultaneous polynomial dependence on genus and finite-field parameters. Fixed genus or small characteristic improvements do not remove unfavorable genus dependence. No low-cost general cohomology algorithm identified.

389257|kedlaya-actual|Hyperelliptic de Rham cup-product question|The source asks whether natural pairings improve computation, rather than asking existence of the pairing. Preserving a symplectic form provides checks but does not alone prove an asymptotic or practical gain. No complete algorithm/complexity bridge identified.

389261|kedlaya-actual|Deformation methods, slide 19|Need a useful nondegenerate deformation plus starting Frobenius matrices and controlled transport. A single easy starting curve or formal interpolation is only a component. Source already reports hyperelliptic implementations; no new full nondegenerate-family mechanism identified.

389272|may|Multivariate modular method, slides 15–16|The body highlights algebraic independence of auxiliary polynomials and optimization of the lattice basis. Determinant inequalities alone are not sufficient to prove resultant elimination succeeds. No full optimality/independence mechanism; no parameter sweep.

389273|may|Coron method, slide 18|The question is dimension reduction for the stated small-root lattice while retaining the recovery bound. Deleting a row/column can remove the vanishing guarantee or worsen the bound. No proof of preserved scope or new reduction mechanism identified.

389275|may|Use bounds constructively, slide 20|The talk already gives an RSA PRNG example and proposes additional primitives from roots beyond the recoverable region. Need an actual reduction under the stated hardness, not just a larger-root label. No full new construction or security proof identified.

389278|montgomery-converted|Five-term GP slides 23–27|The source gives the N=2005 example and a lattice bridge to cubics, but requires avoiding first/second-order recurrences for arbitrary large N. Replaying that example, or using its recurrence-producing prime-N construction, is not the requested fast method. No efficient general GP construction identified.

389279|shparlinski|Group structures question and exponent discussion|The source explicitly says the distribution is not expected uniform. Need specify the curve weighting and derive the full law, not merely demonstrate a bias or cyclic subcase. No new full distribution formula with proof identified.

389289|kedlaya|Howe fixed-field construction slides|The actual body is Howe's talk despite local filename. It reports naive/CM and combined algorithms with field-size rather than polylogarithmic costs. Assignment wording omits efficiency but enumerating all curves is a routine complete adaptation, not a credit-worthy result. Group with C27 instead of inventing a separate outcome.

389290|kedlaya|Howe Broeker–Stevenhagen approach|Allowing the field to vary changes the CM discriminant problem. The source already describes choosing small fundamental discriminant and computing its class polynomial. A new implementation/example of this plan has no novelty; its heuristic efficiency needs successor theorem/proof audit before any investment.

389291|kedlaya|Howe half-open genus-three discussion|The local body asks about a given principally polarized threefold and descent to a Jacobian, whereas the record asks existence somewhere in a Weil-polynomial isogeny class. These are not interchangeable. Polarization, twist and isogeny-existence bridges remain; related context only, no full scope qualification.

389296|kedlaya|Howe final Hermitian-matrix problem|The source explicitly gives the rank-three O_-7 determinant-three lemma and small-rank capabilities. Full question covers every dimension/determinant/PID and sharpness. Generic Minkowski bounds or another tiny case do not deliver the exact sharp function. No cheap uniform extremal mechanism identified.

389298|lange|MNT discussion and open-problems slide 39|More families, embedding degrees and smaller cofactors are a combined design program. The source already discusses MNT methods; a numerical parameter instance is excluded. No new complete family with security and cofactor analysis identified.

389299|lange|Pairing-friendly hyperelliptic context, slide 39|Need suitable curve families, subgroup/security parameters and computable pairings. A curve with a small embedding degree alone is not a complete cryptographic construction. No full-scope low-cost family mechanism identified.

389300|lange|Genus-four tradeoff, slide 39|The request is an exact computational-speed/security tradeoff, requiring both a cost model and best-known attack accounting. A timing benchmark or one parameter instance does not establish it. No rigorous sharp tradeoff mechanism identified.

389301|lange|Break system question, slide 39 and protocol context|The body poses a broad attack challenge, not a single fully quantified theorem. Must identify the specific protocol, parameters and success model before a full resolution. A break of a deliberately weak instance is insufficient; no concrete general attack found.

389302|lange|Security assumptions, slides 40–46|The source distinguishes SDH, Decision Linear and XDH variants and known weakened reductions. Breaking one degenerate instantiation does not determine the weaker assumptions in the intended pairing groups. Taxonomy and successor proof bodies remain unaudited; no new attack mechanism identified.

389306|lange|Pairing Inversion Problems I–II, slides 47–48|The body distinguishes fixed-P, fixed-Q and attacker-chosen arguments. Solving by discrete logarithms is not a hardness classification or efficient inversion. Source reports prior interpolation/multivariate attempts; no new reduction or full algorithm identified.

389310|micciancio|Open problems complexity slide|Cyclic-code minimum distance is distinct from maximum-likelihood decoding for Reed–Solomon codes, which is listed as known. Need preserve cyclicity in the hardness reduction. No such reduction or successor proof audit; not marked publicly solved from analogy.

389313|micciancio|Open problems algorithms slide|The source warns cyclic structure is not preserved by isometries. Rotating a general worst-case LLL basis therefore does not prove an ideal-lattice example with the same behavior. Need an explicit ideal basis and exact LLL trajectory/ratio; no route identified and no search initiated.

389315|micciancio|Open problems cryptography slide|The source already gives one-way/collision-resistant hashes and asks efficient ideal-lattice PRGs. Generic existence from one-way functions needs the full reduction and does not automatically meet intended efficiency. Successor constructions likely require a bounded primary audit; no novelty or resolution asserted here.

389316|micciancio|Open problems cryptography slide|The source separates PRFs from hashes and PRGs. A generic PRF existence argument is not automatically a new efficient ideal-lattice construction. Need concrete parameters and full security reduction plus successor proof audit. No new mechanism qualifies.

389317|micciancio|Open problems cryptography slide|The source specifically asks efficient ideal-lattice signatures. Hash-based signing alone may be routine composition; later direct schemes require primary chronology/security review. No new construction or audited successor proof, so registry/novelty HOLD rather than an open-status inference.

389322|micciancio|Open problems quantum slide|The body lists unit/class-group quantum algorithms as background but asks separately for Smallest Conjugate. Computing units alone does not solve the optimization or certify an efficient reduction. Definition/model and successor proof audit still needed; no concrete quantum mechanism.

389324|micciancio|Open problems quantum slide|Need an efficient ideal-lattice version with the intended quantum-SVP security reduction. Substituting ring notation into Regev's general-lattice scheme does not preserve the reduction. No full construction/reduction; successor literature and registry remain HOLD.

389326|paillier|Instance-malleability definitions and challenge slide 27|n' must be publicly recoverable from n and remain a legitimate generator output with the intended security baseline. n'=n is excluded, n'=n^2 is not a standard RSA semiprime, and exposing a common factor destroys the challenge. No full generator/security mechanism identified.

389327|rivest-converted|Trapdoor DL group slides and summary|The source already cites Dent–Galbraith, Paillier near-misses and pairing constructions with large tables. A known impractical construction or parameter shrink without security proof is not a new practical solution. No compact full mechanism with quantified costs identified.

389328|rivest-converted|GII definitions, known-order caveat and construction slide|The source explicitly hides group order and distinguishes representation/operation feasibility. Exponentiating by a publicly known order-1 is only a conditional observation already in the source, not a refutation. RSA groups have easy inversion as noted there. No reasonable-assumption construction identified.
